content: Patients with angioedema may present with noticeable swelling around the periorbital region and lips. In severe cases, respiratory distress can occur due to edema involving the epiglottis and subglottic tissues. The facial skin, particularly around the mouth, as well as the mucosa of the mouth and throat, and the tongue, may exhibit significant swelling. Urticaria (hives) can develop concurrently, and a rash may also be observed. These findings are consistent with angioedema, as documented in dermatological references. Swelling of the neck may be evident upon examination of the throat. In the lungs, stridor and wheezing may be detected, indicating potential airway involvement. Swelling of the genital region may be observed during abdominal examination. The extremities may also appear swollen. Neurologically, patients may experience slightly reduced sensations in the affected areas, which is likely due to nerve compression caused by the swelling.
